journey.title: Open the filters drawer, land on its autofocus search field, and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: The dialog opens but focus does not move to the autofocus input because the native <dialog> element does not receive focus when shown via showModal() in this environment, causing focus to remain on the triggering button and then be lost to the body.
plan.repair_strategy: After showing the dialog, explicitly focus the element with the autofocus attribute inside the dialog, falling back to the dialog itself.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will move into the dialog and land on the autofocus search field, allowing keyboard users to interact with filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus stealing if the dialog already had focus managed elsewhere, but focusing the autofocus element is harmless and aligns with native behavior.
Risk of focusing a non-visible element if the autofocus attribute is misused, though this is unlikely given the DOM structure.
verification_requirements: After opening the drawer via keyboard, focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Space on #in-stock checkbox toggles its state.
Pressing Tab twice and Enter on #apply updates the applied output to 'in'.
Escape closes drawer and returns focus to #filters-open.

plan.root_cause: The dialog opens via showModal() but focus does not move to the autofocus input because the native <dialog> element does not automatically focus the [autofocus] element when shown via showModal() in this environment, and the synchronous focus() call in _showElement may execute before the dialog is fully in the top layer.
plan.repair_strategy: After showing the dialog in _showElement, schedule a microtask to focus the element with the autofocus attribute inside the dialog, falling back to the dialog itself, ensuring the dialog is fully rendered in the top layer.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will move into the drawer and land on the autofocus search field after a microtask, allowing keyboard users to interact with filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus stealing if the dialog already had focus managed elsewhere, but focusing the autofocus element is harmless and aligns with native behavior.
Risk of focusing a non-visible element if the autofocus attribute is misused, though this is unlikely given the DOM structure.
Microtask delay is negligible but could theoretically allow a race condition if other code moves focus simultaneously.

plan.root_cause: The native <dialog> element does not automatically focus its [autofocus] child when shown via showModal() in this test environment. Synchronous focus() calls in _showElement execute before the dialog is fully in the top layer, and microtask-scheduled focus runs after the test's synchronous assertion check. Focus remains on <body> because the dialog opens but never captures keyboard focus.
plan.repair_strategy: In DialogBase._showElement, after calling showModal(), schedule focus on the [autofocus] element using requestAnimationFrame to ensure the dialog is rendered in the top layer, with a synchronous fallback for environments where rAF runs immediately. This matches Bootstrap's pattern for top-layer focus management.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users opening the filters drawer will land directly on the search field, enabling immediate filter interaction without a pointer.
functional_risks: Minimal timing difference in production (one frame) — negligible for user perception.
If requestAnimationFrame is not available (unlikely), synchronous focus may still race with top-layer entry, but this matches prior behavior.

plan.root_cause: The native <dialog> element does not automatically focus its [autofocus] child when shown via showModal() in this test environment. The _showElement method opens the dialog but does not move focus, leaving it on the triggering element (<body> after Tab key).
plan.repair_strategy: In DialogBase._showElement, after calling showModal() for modal dialogs, synchronously focus the [autofocus] element inside the dialog, falling back to the dialog itself. This ensures keyboard focus lands in the drawer immediately without async timing issues.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users opening the filters drawer will land directly on the search field, enabling immediate filter interaction without a pointer.
functional_risks: Synchronous focus may race with top-layer entry in some environments, but showModal() is synchronous and should establish the top layer first.
If the autofocus element is not focusable (e.g., disabled, hidden), focus() will be a no-op and focus remains on the dialog.
verification_requirements: After opening the drawer via keyboard (Enter on #filters-open), focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Space on #in-stock checkbox toggles its state.
Pressing Tab twice and Enter on #apply updates the applied output to 'in'.
Escape closes drawer and returns focus to #filters-open.
